solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dessert? Unable to finish second course!

indicators.note: a word unable to finish loses its final letter, so the pudding is cut short at its tail

parts.note: a syllabub is a frothy creamed dessert

explanation.surface: A diner, too full to finish pudding, laments that another course is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like part of the meal, but it is a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics in an educational course of study.

clue.text: 7 in play out here

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 7 down, a boy or lad

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue reading as a stage direction about a boy appearing in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The '7' is the answer to 7 down, a boy; the letters run across play, out and here.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young man, the same as a lad.

clue.text: Very much similar to Charles Pooter's job

parts.note: similar to means like
Charles Pooter is the hero of The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith, so he is the Nobody of the title
a job is one's business or line of work

explanation.surface: A literary aside comparing something to the dull clerk's work of a famous comic diarist.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the London clerk who narrates the Victorian comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, so his job is the Nobody's business.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means intensely or to a great degree, as in working hard to an extreme extent.

clue.text: See 3
Stupidly loathes any lowly actor

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters of the following words are arranged in a foolish new order

explanation.surface: A snobbish performer foolishly despises any humble actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Holloway was an English actor and music-hall entertainer, remembered as Alfred Doolittle in My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated English stage and screen performer, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: Parking in Indian city, historic city

indicators.note: in puts the parking letter inside the name of the Indian city

parts.note: Delhi is the Indian capital city
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A traveller notes the parking in an Indian city of great history.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the ancient Greek city famed for its oracle, a classic historic site.

clue.text: Hold back Greek character during row

indicators.note: during puts the Greek letter in the middle of the word for row, as if taking place within it

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man is restrained in the middle of a noisy argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to keep them from leaving, a synonym of holding them back.

clue.text: Boy happy heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: A boy sets off cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad is an everyday synonym for a boy or young man.

clue.text: List of popular songs apartheid affected

indicators.note: affected means acted upon and altered, so the letters of the word are changed in order

explanation.surface: A chart of protest songs influenced by South African apartheid.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the ranked chart of the best-selling pop records.

clue.text: Uproar caused by large number ahead of us

indicators.note: ahead of places the large number in front of the following letters

parts.note: a ruck is a large crowd or mass of people

explanation.surface: A commotion caused by a crowd arriving before we do.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruckus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, a synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Poor diet, not a remedy

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Bad eating habits are not the cure for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is something that counteracts poison or a problem, so a remedy.

clue.text: Poor article, not good

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for good is to be left out of the word for article

parts.note: a thing is an article or object

explanation.surface: A shop item is of low quality and no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is not a grammatical article like THE but an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin can mean poor or inadequate, as in a thin excuse or thin evidence.

clue.text: Danielle, distraught after one has rejected love — music hall song

indicators.note: after says the rearranged name comes behind the shortened word
has rejected means the zero letter is thrown out of the word for one

parts.note: the word one taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in disorder, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Danielle is heartbroken after someone has spurned her love, and a song is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has rejected' drops O from ONE leaving NE; 'distraught' turns DANIELLE into LLIEDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nellie Dean is a famous Edwardian sentimental ballad sung in British music halls and pubs.

clue.text: Sketch popular stable lad in reception area

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
in means fashionable or popular
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A drawing of a well-liked stable hand is displayed in a hotel lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room is a formal room in a house for receiving and entertaining guests.

clue.text: Mistake wearing gemstone of poor quality

indicators.note: wearing means the mistake has the gemstone around it like clothing

parts.note: a ruby is a red gemstone
bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: An error made while wearing a jewel leads to shoddy results.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbishy is informal for worthless or shoddy, describing low-grade goods.

clue.text: Roof of library in complex done up, is as good as new

indicators.note: in puts the top letter inside the rearranged letters
complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up
roof of means the top letter of a down entry, so the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The renovated top floor of a library building now looks brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' shuffles DONE UP IS into UNSPOIED, and 'in' puts the L from 'Roof of library' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoiled is undamaged and pristine, so it remains in mint condition.

clue.text: An element of political asylum, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: An element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully admits a political asylum claim has an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used like the phrase unfortunately or sadly.

clue.text: Unable to manage without servants?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the word means lacking help, that is with no domestic staff

explanation.surface: A householder wonders whether they could cope with no domestic staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition also reads literally as lacking servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpless means powerless or incapable of coping on one's own.

clue.text: Employed American editor

explanation.surface: An American newspaper editor has been hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' reads as hired, but the sense needed is put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means put to use, which is what employed means of a tool or method.

clue.text: Quip about English ship

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on art
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A witty remark is made concerning an English vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short joke or witty remark, the same thing as a quip.

clue.text: Serious pest that woman? On the contrary

parts.note: a rat is a serious vermin pest
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being a nasty pest, and replies that she is, not him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reads like the accused's retort but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather can introduce a correction meaning instead or more precisely, as on the contrary does.

clue.text: Small beer after fish and gammon

indicators.note: after puts the small beer behind the fish

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A pub meal of fish and ham with a half of beer to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gammon' looks like ham, but here it is old slang for nonsense; WALLOP is British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is dated British slang for humbug or nonsense, and codswallop means nonsense too.

clue.text: Old German understood by husband

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so got means understood

explanation.surface: An elderly German man is understood by her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were an ancient Germanic people, so a Goth was an early German.

clue.text: Hope to extend business credit to self-governing hospital

definitions.meaning: to hope something is so is to ... it will be
to ... a customer is to give goods on credit
a self-governing body running hospitals in Britain

explanation.surface: A hospital hopes to borrow money to stay independent.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; in Britain's National Health Service, hospitals are run by self-governing bodies called trusts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hoping, lending on credit, and a self-governing NHS hospital body.

clue.text: Form of comic verse member of the clergy abridged, then cut

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the clergyman word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: A churchman's comic poem is shortened and then edited.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a four-line humorous biographical poem, a recognised type of light verse.

clue.text: Rubbish to right to be tipped

indicators.note: tipped means turned over, so the down entry is reversed

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right; that the letters also run backwards across the clue words is a coincidence of the word to plus R

explanation.surface: Waste needs tipping on the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' suggests dumping rubbish, but turns TOR upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot means nonsense or worthless talk, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Used at sea to carry ten over in mass migration

indicators.note: to carry means the jumbled letters hold the other pieces inside them
at sea means confused, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A ship was used to carry many people across in a great migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns USED into EDUS, which carries XO after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a large departure of people, as in the Israelites leaving Egypt.

clue.text: Journalist cycled back carrying it

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the following word inside it
back says the word for cycled is read in reverse

parts.note: rode means cycled, as on a bicycle

explanation.surface: A reporter rode home with something on the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RODE into EDOR, which carries IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper journalist who prepares and selects copy.

clue.text: See toy I'm flying in National Park

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A child invites a parent to watch a toy plane flying in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a celebrated US national park in California.
